section1.p: Unsubmitted, unnumbered ProtoXEP draft, version 0.0.2. It has not been accepted or approved by the XMPP Standards Foundation. urn:xmpp:polls:0 is a proposed namespace and discovery feature, not an assigned registration.

This revision proposes structured XML. Monogram 0.2.195 at commit 4736f7eddb423192e5d68435879f0b0a88371168 implements the earlier body-parsing convention, not this proposal. Development source now includes shared Java/Rust structured codecs, protected-content allowlists and wire/crypto vectors. Mobile structured receive/storage/voting and desktop direct authoring are being integrated. Native mobile authoring/update/forward/outbox migration remains incomplete; this is not a claim that 0.2.195 ships the revised format.

XEP-0444 already supplies reaction sets and mentions voting as a use case. This profile adds a recognizable poll definition, option mapping and tally semantics without requiring a poll server. It does not create anonymous votes, quizzes or server-enforced elections. When the optional readable fallback is supplied, a text-only client can read the poll and use its reaction picker.

A poll is one direct poll child in urn:xmpp:polls:0. Its required type is single or multiple. It contains exactly one question, zero or one description, and an ordered list of option children in that namespace. Each option has a required emoji attribute and its label as text. An optional closed boolean defaults to false. Receivers MUST derive all poll state from this structured payload; they MUST NOT parse the message body for questions, options, mappings, mode or closure.

ul.li: Require 2–32 options. Question and optional description are bounded to 4096 Unicode scalar values each; option labels to 1024. The serialized UTF-8 poll element MUST NOT exceed 65536 bytes. These are independent safety bounds, not encryption-version limits.

Fields MUST contain non-whitespace text, with no nested markup or invalid XML characters. Option emoji must be valid under XEP-0444 and unique after removing U+FE0F. Senders choose their emoji mapping; receivers MUST NOT infer it from position or a fixed emoji table.

Validate the complete definition before showing voting controls. Duplicate questions or emoji, unknown modes, malformed booleans, multiple poll elements and exceeded bounds MUST NOT produce a partial or guessed poll.
No native Telegram ID, serialized application object or binary option ID is transmitted. Future incompatible changes require a new namespace version.

example.caption: Structured poll with an optional readable fallback

section1.example:
<message xmlns='jabber:client' to='room@example.org' type='groupchat' id='poll-123'> <body>📊 Where shall we eat?
1️⃣ Pizza 2️⃣ Noodles 3️⃣ Sushi
React with an option's emoji to vote. Choose one.</body> <poll xmlns='urn:xmpp:polls:0' type='single'> <question>Where shall we eat?</question> <option emoji='1️⃣'>Pizza</option> <option emoji='2️⃣'>Noodles</option> <option emoji='3️⃣'>Sushi</option> </poll> <fallback xmlns='urn:xmpp:fallback:0' for='urn:xmpp:polls:0'> <body/> </fallback> </message>

example.caption: The same poll without a body or fallback

section1.example: <message xmlns='jabber:client' to='room@example.org' type='groupchat' id='poll-124'> <poll xmlns='urn:xmpp:polls:0' type='single'> <question>Where shall we eat?</question> <option emoji='1️⃣'>Pizza</option> <option emoji='2️⃣'>Noodles</option> <option emoji='3️⃣'>Sushi</option> </poll> </message>
section1.p: The body fallback is OPTIONAL and MAY be localized. Its wording, numbering, indentation and line endings are not protocol tokens. Changing or omitting it does not change the structured poll. When included, XEP-0428 marks the redundant text for urn:xmpp:polls:0. A client MUST suppress a marked fallback only after successfully understanding and rendering the structured poll. Invalid or unsupported metadata MUST NOT hide readable fallback text. An unmarked body is ordinary accompanying text and MUST NOT be silently hidden. Unsupported body-less content should be visibly identified as unsupported, not silently discarded.

A ballot is an XEP-0444 replacement set targeted to the original message ID in a direct conversation, or a stable room-assigned stanza ID in a MUC. Use the authenticated actor and conversation under the reaction transport rules. One actor has one current complete replacement set; retain non-option reactions. Ignore U+FE0F when comparing option emoji. A single-choice set with two or more distinct option emoji is invalid and contributes no ballot. An empty option subset withdraws the ballot. Multiple choice counts one voter in the total and one vote for each selected option.
section1.example: <message xmlns='jabber:client' from='juliet@example.org/phone' to='room@example.org' type='groupchat'> <reactions xmlns='urn:xmpp:reactions:0' id='room-assigned-poll-id'> <reaction>2️⃣</reaction> </reactions> </message>
section1.p: Persist reaction events so that a vote received before its poll or via archive replay can be reconciled. Duplicate events must not add votes. Actor identity must survive nickname changes; an anonymous room without a stable authorized actor binding cannot provide attributable public ballots. This compatibility profile inherits the deployed reaction journal order; it does not claim an independently specified global order for equal-time conflicting replacements. That ordering is a standards-track design issue.

Only an author-authenticated XEP-0308 correction with unchanged question, description, ordered options/emoji mapping and mode, and closed set to true, closes a poll. The corrected structured definition MUST be complete; a sentence in the body does not authorize closure. Its optional fallback MAY be updated to explain closure.

A local accepted-timestamp cutoff is not a server-enforced deadline. Delay timestamps and clock differences are not cryptographic proof of when a vote was cast. Globally convergent ordering for equal-time replacements and strict closure remains an explicit review issue. Forwarding creates a new open poll with a new message identity and no copied ballots.

Conforming clients MUST advertise urn:xmpp:polls:0 using XEP-0030, in addition to independently implemented XEP-0444 support. Advertising this feature requires support for definitions without a body. No support is inferred from a body prefix. Malformed message payloads must not trigger automatic error-message loops, external fetches or refresh requests.

OMEMO 2 (urn:xmpp:omemo:2, XEP-0384) can protect the poll XML inside the content of the Stanza Content Encryption envelope defined by XEP-0420 and the OMEMO SCE profile. A readable fallback and its XEP-0428 marker, if included, belong inside that same protected content. A fallback-less poll can be encrypted identically. Question, choices, emoji mapping and closure state MUST NOT be duplicated as unprotected outer hints. Ballots and corrections require the same authenticated-content protection in an encrypted conversation.

Body-only legacy OMEMO is not a constraint on this format. Clients MUST NOT silently move structured poll or ballot data outside encryption, or serialize authoritative options into a body to compensate. Explain when the selected encryption mode cannot support the feature. An explicitly chosen text-only compatibility send remains ordinary text, not a structured poll.
Unsupported anonymous, hidden-results, media-option, quiz, audience or authoritative timed-close requests must be rejected rather than claiming those properties.

The two creation examples above MUST produce identical questions, modes, options and emoji mappings. Translating, modifying or deleting the marked fallback MUST leave that result unchanged. Both clients must verify body-less delivery, persistence and replay, malformed/duplicate options and variation-selector aliases, replacement votes and withdrawal, authenticated closure, foreign targets and protected XML round trips. Existing legacy body-parser tests alone do not satisfy these requirements. Development source now accepts validated poll XML in protected content, with Java/Rust vectors and native receive tests; mobile authoring/update/outbox and complete cross-client UI acceptance remain open.

A supporting client MUST expose question, labels, selection, counts and closure as text to assistive technology even when no body fallback exists. Color, animation and emoji MUST NOT be the sole labels for voting controls. Accessible local presentation is required; a wire body fallback is optional.

Question, description and labels are Unicode. Protocol names and type values are case-sensitive; human-facing fallback prose is not a wire grammar and MAY be localized. Bounds use Unicode scalar values and UTF-8 bytes as specified, not implementation-dependent UTF-16 units.

Receivers MUST validate the complete bounded representation before treating it as structured data. A sender-controlled label or body prefix does not authenticate a different author. Private native IDs and serialized application objects MUST NOT be accepted from the network. No received content authorizes a local action without the normal user authorization.

Votes and voter identities are public to the conversation. Encryption protects them from outsiders only to the extent supplied by the selected transport. Hiding option reaction chips in a native card does not hide ballots from other participants or erase the event journal.
This document requests no IANA action. No media type or URI scheme is registered by publication of this draft.

This draft proposes urn:xmpp:polls:0 as an XML namespace and discovery feature. It is not registered by creating this draft; final allocation/versioning requires XSF review. No assigned number or short name is claimed.

The following pinned sources implement the historical body-only convention, not this revised structured proposal. Their tests are legacy behavior evidence. Development source adds the structured codec, persistence and OMEMO 2 allowlist support. Mobile authoring, updates, forwarding and outbox integration still require completion before its namespace advertisement. The legacy codec remains explicitly separate during migration.
